close inspection reveals that a majority (~90%) of the plots show scratch marks on the material that was blocking escape, or signs of attempted tunneling to the surface

So…buried immortals. Immortals buried alive?

If they were buried alive, why did they die? Obviously, the "keeper" only "captured" these immortals before interring them. So if the keeper didn't kill the immortals:

  1. How were they captured and interred?
  2. What eventually killed them? Lack of air/food/water? Inability to re-up on immortality juice?
  3. Are any of the immortals buried here still alive?

I realize the SCP entry as it stands should remain unable to answer these queries, unless researchers are able to directly observe and document the processes in question. It still leaves me curious though.

Curiosity earns this a +1 for leaving me wanting more, without leaving me wishing there was more to this entry.

Hmm. If the foundation regularly re-uses designations, then I do agree with you.

Well, designations on the site are "re-used" when articles are deleted due to low ratings. (So if someone wrote a new SCP article but its rating fell below -10, the SCP's numerical designation would be open for someone else to write an article for that number, even though the number had already been used.)

Sometimes articles in series 1 will be found to not conform to current site standards, and so the article is reviewed and then rewritten or deleted. As such, references sometimes remain.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
"I don't think theres anything wrong with my sentence structure besides being longer( and can someone tell me if there is? from what I've seen from the comments, a lot of people say they like the idea in a strange way "from what i could gather" "from what i saw". Is that the same as saying "from what i understood"? is my writing complete gibberish? i can handle my formatting not being appropriate for this site, but it would really disturb me if my writing is universally bad) but see now that the bullets are a much better way to do things."

I know you say this is your informal writing, but ironically, your question is the best example of what's wrong with your overall sentence structure (as per the article pre-rewrite). You miss commas, and often string many complex phrases together before ending a statement. Also, the way you order your ideas can be confusing at times. Here's a quick rewrite:

"The rewrite's example showed me that a bulleted list is a much better way to do things. Before, I didn't think there was anything wrong with my sentence structure, though I do tend to write longer sentences than others. However, from what I've seen of these comments, even those who liked the idea use phrases like "from what I could gather", or "from what I saw". Is that like saying "from what I understood", as if it were hard to decipher? Is my writing complete gibberish? I can handle the idea that my formatting wasn't appropriate for this site, but it would really disturb me if my writing was universally bad."

Now, I don't mean to insult you, here. The reason I took the time to edit this article is because your idea was excellent; it was just that the grammar, organization, and style was right-out. So, since I'm a grammar nazi and hate to see a great idea downrated and gone to waste, I did the best I could.

Many of your ideas - especially your color and suppositions - took up too much space in each sentence. I didn't completely remove them, however: many I simply compressed into analytical adjectives, reducing clutter and improving the scientific tone without removing information. For example, "the team ventures to guess that this is it's way of gloating" was compressed within the statement that the inscriber "eagerly takes responsibility" for the deaths of its victims. I'm sorry if it seems like the color was drained out of the article, but we could always add an incident report of a grave being added. That would add plenty of colorful dialogue and [DATA EXPUNGED].

Your fake hero "Calothisosi of Britannica" seems kind of random, especially since he's fake. If you don't mind, I'm going to go ahead and replace him with Achilles. And by "Christ's two graves", I meant an empty one inscribed "not even you are above me", and a full one inscribed something like "oops, i forgot to lock the first one". The significance would be that it involves the only grave without a corpse in it, giving us the perfect place to insert it in the article. Again, it's more funny than scary, so never mind.

item.content:encoded:
i was actually going to try to refute all of clef's points and offer a opposite opinion (and then leave the site, don't worry, I'm not one of those guys who will hold completely differing ideas against the consensus and then remain, stubbornly refusing to change, continuing to post articles that annoy everyone, and being a general pain in the side. i have more style then that) but then i saw how excellent the rewrite was, and that gave me hope. Or maybe i just have more patience then i thought. (no need to huff, "why does he need patience, he's the one trying us" i don't mean i need patience for the people here, but more for the frustration caused by the disparity between my expectations of everyone loving my articles, and what actually happed (getting severely down rated.. ouch!) A lesser men would of become ill tempered by now (or maybe a lesser men would of said a lesser man would of become ill tempered by now, and then act self righteous that he was actually taking everything in stride :)

Ok, anyways, one thing that really stuck with me were the bullets. I don't think theres anything wrong with my sentence structure besides being longer( and can someone tell me if there is? from what I've seen from the comments, a lot of people say they like the idea in a strange way "from what i could gather" "from what i saw". Is that the same as saying "from what i understood"? is my writing complete gibberish? i can handle my formatting not being appropriate for this site, but it would really disturb me if my writing is universally bad) but see now that the bullets are a much better way to do things.

I was debating leaving out "the team ventures to guess that this is it's way of gloating" but i decided that i really wanted to point people in that direction of thought. Was it so wrong to keep that in their. Can't something be clinical (lacking emotion) while still drawing hypothesis? i mean their scientists, right. thats what scientists do. (this is one of the points i was going to say to clef, although in a more likely ruder and huffier manner (at least thats how it sounded in my head when planning it out) (i'm sorry clef, your doing a great job, and I'm really thankful for your help, but when people stumble across their article with -3, strange thoughts kick around in their heads while the blood drains from their face)

well, i go nothing else to say right now. I'm going to attempt to become better (don't worry, after reading this comment and slap your head "he hasn't learned anything, look at it it's all one giant run on sentence" i always write like this when informal, and don't even try to make sense of it, it's all stream of conscious) and go with the flow. i hope this all works out, because i got some really sweat ideas coming up.

P.S

Calothisosi of Britannica is a made out figure, a sort of fake Celtic hero type. It stands to reason that we wouldn't know all the immortals who existed so while reading the article we could hear of one that we're never heard of before, so i just made him up. also i couldn't think of a "real" immortal who was invulnerable. there's a small list of real life immortals on wikipedia "list of immortals" is anyones interested.

Whats are you talking about when you mention Jesus' two graves? is it one of your ideas? because in mine, jesus christ was only implied to be in the trophy crypt (which i think is a great ending line. I'm glad you didn't take it out. really creepy. sums up the hopelessness. this thing kills even the divine, or maybe even reached into heaven.)

Kill the easter bunny instead. santa's actually pretty cool, the easter bunny on the other hand, is the dumbest idea in the world. maybe we could have it show up in the graveyard and replace it with a giant chicken, which makes marginally more sense.
